title: Stochastic Order Learning: An Approach to Rank Estimation Using Noisy Data
claim: Unlike nominal classification, ordinal rank labels carry noise whose severity varies, so some label errors are far worse than others.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, image columns over true/noisy label rows, severity color bar
description: The figure has two side-by-side panels. The left panel is labeled for nominal classification. It shows three photos (a Shiba-like dog, a chow dog, a bear cub) under a pale, nearly uniform 'Noise severity' bar. Below each photo is a true label (Dog, Dog, Bear) and a red noisy label (Cat, Bear, Dog). All errors sit at the same faint severity because class labels have no order. The right panel is for ordered data in rank estimation. It shows three face photos with true ages 24, 53 and 43 and noisy ages 26, 63 and 59. Its severity bar is a gradient from white to deep red. Pins from each face point to positions on the bar, and larger age errors land at redder positions. The eye goes first to the red gradient bar and the red noisy labels.
caption: Nominal data in classification versus ordered data in rank estimation. Unlike classification, in rank estimation, certain errors are severer than others.
abstract: Rank estimation under label noise poses a fundamental challenge, as ordinal annotations often exhibit structured uncertainty rather than simple label corruption. In this paper, we reformulate rank estimation with noisy ordinal labels as a stochastic ordering problem, in which each instance is inherently associated with multiple plausible ranks instead of a single deterministic label. Based on this view, we propose stochastic order learning (SOL), a learning framework that captures ordinal label uncertainty and learns an embedding space through two complementary objectives: a discriminative loss that structures instance--centroid interactions and a stochastic order loss that enforces probabilistic ordering relations between instances. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate that SOL enables reliable rank estimation under various types and levels of label noise. The source code is available at https://github.com/cwlee00/SOL.
